Just ahead of Apple’s special event, Bloomberg has published a new report detailing the decade-long development of Apple’s foldable iPhone.

The report specifically mentions former Apple CEO Tim Cook’s involvement in the project and reveals the possible price of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman says Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after returning from a trip to China, Cook was said to be “unusually excited” about foldable phones. According to reports, he pushed Apple’s hardware team to accelerate the development of the company’s first foldable product.

Cook generally “does not participate in the conception of new products,” so his personal involvement in the foldable iPhone’s development has added considerable weight to the project:

As for the pricing of the foldable iPhone (referred to internally throughout Apple as the iPhone Ultra), the company’s original target was an entry-level price of US$1,999. However, due to recent increases in component costs, the target price has been revised to US$2,199.

Some versions with larger storage capacities may approach US$3,000. By comparison, the standard iPhone currently starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be on the ground at the Steve Jobs Theater, bringing you in-depth coverage of everything.
